prototype.headline: You can register a Xero app and test with a demo company the same day.

production.handsOnTime: unknown until certification questionnaire is prepared
production.headline: Public launch may require app certification and tier upgrade, which involves a review process.

verdict.confidence: high on documented OAuth, redirect URI and tier rules; medium on certification timeline
verdict.summary: Xero offers a self‑serve OAuth registration for testing, but a production launch that exceeds the free Starter tier or uses premium features triggers a security assessment and app certification review that can take several weeks.

steps.text: Count the number of organisations that will connect. If ≤5 you can stay in the free Starter tier; otherwise you must select Core or higher.

stages.name: Sign up for a Xero developer account

steps.text: Create a free Xero account and log into the Xero Developer Portal.
In the Developer Portal click **Create App**, give it a name, and submit. You will receive a client ID and client secret.
Add up to 50 redirect URIs (no wildcards allowed). Each must be an absolute HTTPS URL.
For native or mobile apps use the Authorization Code flow with PKCE; single‑page apps are not supported.
Use the Xero demo company and API Explorer to exercise the OAuth flow and API calls without charge.

stages.name: Upgrade tier / request premium features (if needed)

steps.text: If you need more than 5 connections or need premium endpoints (e.g., Journals, XPM API, Bulk Connections), select Core, Plus, Advanced or Enterprise tier and prepare for a security assessment.

stages.name: Submit for app certification (required for Core+ tiers)

steps.text: Complete the Xero app certification questionnaire and submit it via the Developer Portal. The provider will review and may request additional information.

requirements: Registered OAuth app with client ID and client secret
Redirect URIs (HTTPS, up to 50, no wildcards)
User with Standard, Adviser or Administrator role to authorize the connection
Compliance with Xero’s tiered pricing model (Starter, Core, Plus, Advanced, Enterprise)
If using premium endpoints, a security assessment and use‑case approval (Advanced tier or higher)
App certification for Core tier and above

blockers.issue: No dynamic client registration endpoint; app must be created manually in the portal.
blockers.whenItHits: Immediately – you cannot auto‑register an app via metadata.
blockers.whatToDo: Create the app manually in the Xero Developer Portal.

blockers.issue: Exceeding the free Starter tier connection limit (5) blocks additional organisations.
blockers.whenItHits: When you try to connect a 6th organisation.
blockers.whatToDo: Upgrade to Core tier (or higher) and provide a credit‑card for billing.

blockers.issue: Access to premium endpoints (Journals, XPM API, Bulk Connections) requires a security assessment.
blockers.whenItHits: When you attempt to call those endpoints without the required tier.
blockers.whatToDo: Apply for the Advanced tier and complete the security assessment.

blockers.issue: App certification review may delay production launch.
blockers.whenItHits: After you submit the certification questionnaire.
blockers.whatToDo: Prepare documentation, answer the questionnaire, and wait for provider review.

agentCanDo: Generate a Composio Connect Link with the registered client ID/secret
Poll the connection status until ACTIVE
Run test API calls against the demo company and report results
Pre‑fill the certification questionnaire with known app details
youMustDo: Create a Xero developer account and register the OAuth app
Provide the redirect URIs and configure PKCE if needed
Supply a credit‑card for paid tiers and accept the new developer terms
Respond to any security‑assessment requests and provide use‑case justification

claims.text: Xero supports OAuth 2.0 and requires it for all new integrations.
Wildcards are not supported in redirect URIs; each must be an absolute URI.
You can register up to 50 redirect URIs for a Xero app.
Access tokens expire after 30 minutes; unused refresh tokens expire after 60 days.
Xero supports PKCE for native apps; single‑page apps are not currently supported.
Rate limits: 5 concurrent calls, 60 calls per minute, 5 000 calls per day per connection; 10 000 calls per minute across all connections.
Starting 2 Mar 2026 Xero moves to tiered pricing (Starter, Core, Plus, Advanced, Enterprise) with connection limits (5, 50, 1 000, 10 000, unlimited).
Certain app types (e.g., bespoke integrations, custom connections, financial services, conversion partners, franchise apps) are excluded from the new pricing model.
The Journals endpoint, Xero Practice Manager API, and Bulk Connections require a security assessment and use‑case approval, available only from the Advanced tier.
Xero provides an app certification process for Core, Plus, Advanced, and Enterprise tiers.
The user authorising the connection must have Standard, Adviser, or Administrator role with the Connected Apps permission.
To use the Xero API you must register an app to obtain a client ID and client secret; basic API‑key authentication is not supported.
The quickest way to try the API is to set up a demo company and use the API Explorer; there is no charge for the demo company.
Xero does not expose a well‑known OAuth metadata endpoint; dynamic client registration is not advertised.
Composio's XERO toolkit lists auth OAUTH2; Composio-managed OAuth available: no.

nextAction: Create a Xero developer account, register your OAuth app, configure redirect URIs, and test against the demo company. If you need more than 5 connections or premium features, plan for a tier upgrade and the certification review.
composioTail: In the Composio dashboard go to Auth Configs, click Create Auth Config, select the toolkit and choose OAuth2.
Copy the redirect URI shown in the Composio dashboard and register it in the provider's app settings.
Copy the Client ID and Client Secret from the provider app overview into the Composio auth config, and click Create.
Copy the resulting auth config ID (looks like ac_xxxx). Keep secrets out of source control.
Pass the auth config ID to your session: authConfigs: { [toolkit]: 'ac_xxxx' }. Toolkits not listed keep using Composio managed auth.
